Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for standing by. I'm Polina, your Chorus Call operator. Welcome, and thank you for joining Turkcell's conference call and live webcast to present and discuss the Turkcell third quarter 2026 financial results. [Operator Instructions] The conference is being recorded. [Operator Instructions] At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Mrs. Ozlem Yardim, Investor Relations and Corporate Finance Director. Ms. Yardim, you may now proceed.

Ozlem Yardim: Thank you, Polina. Good evening, everyone, and welcome to Turkcell's 2026 Third Quarter Earnings Call. Before we begin, I would like to kindly remind you to review our safe harbor statement, which is available at the end of our presentation. Our earnings release and today's presentation are available on our Investor Relations website. Our CEO, Mr. Ali Taha Koc, will begin with an overview of our business performance, followed by our CFO, Mr. Kamil Kalyon, who will take you through our financial results. After the presentation, we will open the line for your questions. It is now my pleasure to hand over to our CEO, Mr. Ali Taha Koc.

Ali Koç: Thank you very much, Ozlem. Good evening, everyone. Welcome to Turkcell's third quarter 2026 results call. I will start with our operational and strategic highlights, and Kamil will walk you through the financial results. We will then open the floor for questions. We delivered an outstanding quarter, combining robust real revenue growth and excellent execution across our businesses. These results bolster our confidence in achieving our full year real revenue growth and EBITDA margin guidance. Let me now share our key achievements. Our strategy -- growth strategy once again translated into excellent results this quarter. Consolidated revenues reached TRY 82 billion, representing 6.2% year-on-year growth in real terms. This reflects disciplined execution and the growing contribution from our diversified businesses.

Our targeted pricing actions will increasingly translate into ARPU growth as postpaid contracts are renewed. Assuming inflation remains in line with our expectations, we anticipate an acceleration in real ARPU growth over the coming quarters. Beyond our commercial performance, our network leadership remains a key competitive advantage. On April 1, we marked a major milestone with the launch of 5G in Turkiye. Carrying forward our speed leadership from the 4.5G era, Turkcell is once again delivering the highest 5G speeds. Our superior network capabilities are also a key strength behind Superbox, our market-leading Fixed Wireless Access offering. Superbox extends our broadband reach beyond our fiber footprint and continues to lead the Fixed Wireless Access market.

In the first 9 months of 2026 alone, our solar energy portfolio generated TRY 286 million in OpEx saving. As additional capacity comes online, we expect these savings to grow further. With Turkiye hosting COP31 this month, our progress in renewable energy reflects our commitment to turning sustainability ambitions into concrete action, while creating long-term value for our business. Let's now turn to Digital Business Services, one of the key contributors to this quarter's performance. Digital Business Services posted an outstanding quarter. Revenues reached TRY 10.5 billion, up 65% year-on-year, now accounting for nearly 13% of group revenues. The business has firmly established itself as a major contributor to Turkcell's overall performance.

Large-scale project renewals made a significant contribution to this quarter's growth. Beyond these renewals, customer demand remained robust across our digital solution portfolio. In our data center and cloud businesses, global RAM and memory supply constraints and geopolitical uncertainties have led to some delays in customer demand, creating a more challenging environment than initially anticipated. As a result, we expect a more gradual revenue growth trajectory this year. Our data center business continues to advance. We now have 54 megawatts of active IT capacity across 4 locations. Construction of the hyperscale data center facilities in Ankara for Google Cloud's Turkiye region is progressing at a rapid pace. I want to emphasize the strategic importance of data center investments.

With TRY 628 million invested to date in the data center and hyperscale infrastructure, we are building the foundation for our next phase of cloud and digital service growth, both for Turkiye and Turkcell. Our ambitions go well beyond traditional cloud services. We are advancing our work on GPU-based cloud offering and next-generation artificial intelligence infrastructure, so that we are ready to capture new opportunities as enterprise demand for AI accelerates. Our commercial performance was equally impressive. We secured 1,393 new contracts in Q3, bringing our system integration backlog to TRY 21.6 billion. This substantial backlog offers clear visibility into our future revenue potential.

As we expand our digital capabilities, Techfin gives us another way to enhance customer engagement and diversify our revenues. Our Techfin business made a substantial contribution to group revenues, driven by another strong quarter from Paycell. Paycell has an impressive pace of growth, with revenue increasing 23% year-on-year to TRY 2.9 billion. Nongroup revenues accounted for 81% of the total, demonstrating Paycell's global market reach and its ability to scale well beyond the Turkcell ecosystem. Pay later transaction volumes grew 54%, while POS transaction volumes increased 94%, driving POS revenues to an all-time high. The POS business strengthens Paycell's position in the digital payments market. Paycell expands its reach, growing its active user base to 7.1 million users.

Financell also gained momentum with 3% quarter-on-quarter revenue growth in real terms. Looking ahead, the recent increase in the device price limit for 12-month installment plans from TRY 20,000 to TRY 40,000 creates further opportunities for growth in Q4. Our loan portfolio maintained healthy growth, reaching TRY 10.7 billion. Meanwhile, lower funding costs and our prudent risk-based pricing strategy underpinned a net interest margin of 7.7%. Financell maintained its leadership in the consumer finance market with a 43% market share by number of loans. Our expanding base of 16.3 million preapproved credit customers further strengthens our growth potential. Beyond our business performance, Turkcell is also taking a more prominent role on the global technology stage.

I am proud to have been appointed Chair of the GSMA Technology Group and reelected to the GSMA Board. These roles give us a stronger voice in shaping the future of our industry, particularly in 5G, 6G, artificial intelligence, and next-generation networks, while elevating Turkcell's international standing and Turkiye's role in the broader digital ecosystem. Let me close with a final message. Step by step, we are building the Turkcell of tomorrow, a diversified technology company that combines leadership in connectivity with cutting-edge digital infrastructure, next-generation cloud, and artificial intelligence capabilities we are investing in today. These investments range from GPU-based cloud to AI-ready data centers.

Artificial intelligence will define the next decade of this industry, and our investments put us at the center of it in Turkiye. That is how we will capture new opportunities, deliver sustainable and profitable growth, and create lasting value for our shareholders. And with that, let me hand it over to Kamil, who will take you through our financial performance.

Kamil Kalyon: Thank you, Ali Taha Koc. Let me turn to our third quarter financial results. It was another excellent quarter for Turkcell. Building on our strong first half performance, we accelerated revenue growth and delivered further improvement in profitability. Our disciplined pricing strategy, together with robust momentum in our corporate business, was instrumental in delivering these results. This performance underscores the strength of our diversified business model and our continued focus on profitable growth. Group revenue reached TRY 82 billion, representing an impressive year-on-year increase of 6.2%. Turkcell Turkiye remains the primary engine of group growth, supported by accelerating activity in the corporate segment. Meanwhile, consumer revenues returned to positive growth, supported by our pricing actions and increasingly rational market dynamics.

This marks an important turning point, signaling positive shift in the segment's growth trajectory. Turning to profitability, I would like to highlight 2 key achievements. First, we expanded our EBITDA margin despite a higher revenue contribution from hardware sales in the corporate segment and POS services, both of which carry structurally lower margins. Second, and perhaps even more notably, this improvement came on top of an already exceptional EBITDA margin of 43.9% in the same quarter last year. As a result, we achieved an outstanding EBITDA margin of 44.2%, exceeding expectations and further demonstrating our ability to deliver profitable growth through disciplined execution. Next slide, please. Moving to net income.

Let me walk you through the main factors driving this quarter's results. The amortization of 5G license accounted for approximately half of the year-on-year increase in depreciation. At the same time, the capitalized license continued to generate significant monetary gains, providing a favorable offset. On the financing side, our net FX loss was driven by several factors, including outstanding 5G license installments, higher year-on-year TL depreciation, and a larger short FX position amid elevated hedging costs. To mitigate the impact of rising foreign exchange losses, we closely monitor market conditions and dynamically manage our cash position by taking proactive measures to capture favorable opportunities. In this context, our FX swap transactions have enabled us to generate substantial interest income.

Our net financial income, excluding FX loss, reached a positive TRY 2.1 billion, representing a 3.5-fold increase compared to same period last year. Turning to our equity accounted investments, TOGG continued to make encouraging operational progress as it scaled up its business. Its impact on group net income improved by TRY 367 million year-on-year. This progress further reinforces our confidence in its long-term potential. Our tax expense also declined meaningfully year-on-year, reflecting the favorable impact of fixed asset revaluation. Taken together, these factors resulted in net income of TRY 6.7 billion for the quarter. Next slide please. Let me now take you through our capital expenditure performance.

Our operational CapEx to sales ratio stood at 22.2% in the third quarter and 22.8% for the first 9 months of 2026, both below our full year guidance of 25%. We remain on track to meet our full year targets. We allocated 82% of our operational CapEx to mobile and fixed infrastructure, focusing on enhancing network capabilities and extending our fiber reach. A portion of our planned CapEx for data center and renewable energy projects has shifted to subsequent periods following adjustments to project execution schedules. Our fiber rollout gained further momentum during the quarter. In the first 9 months of 2026, we added 574,000 new home passes, expanding our total fiber footprint to 6.9 million.

With our superior infrastructure and the wider spectrum portfolio, we are best positioned to deliver the leading 5G experience in Turkiye. We continue to expand our 5G site footprint this quarter. Turning to our data center investment, we activated the last module of our data center in Ankara as outlined last quarter. Meanwhile, construction of our data center facilities under the Google Cloud partnership is progressing steadily, with the first module scheduled for delivery in 2028. Next slide, please. Turning to our balance sheet. We closed the quarter with TRY 99 billion in cash, maintaining a strong liquidity position and ample financial flexibility to pursue our strategic priorities.

Net debt increased compared to year-end 2025, mainly reflecting the first 5G license installment, including VAT, the annual wireless usage fee, bonus payment and higher capital expenditures. Nevertheless, our leverage improved quarter-on-quarter, with net debt-to-EBITDA declining 0.31x, remaining comfortably below peer levels. Looking ahead, the fourth quarter marks an important phase in our strategic investment journey, including the acquisition of our new headquarters and an increased stake in TOGG. These investments reinforce our long-term commitment to strengthening Turkcell's strategic positioning and growth potential. In particular, the acquisition of our new headquarters, spanning a gross area of 83,000 square meters, represent an attractive investment, combining a prime location with a favorable purchase price.

Beyond its financial merits, the new premises will serve as a technology and innovation hub, fostering closer collaboration and accelerating product development. In parallel, we have already initiated projects to unlock value from our existing real estate portfolio, and we will continue to explore further value creation opportunities. This demonstrates our ability to fund significant investments, capture long-term growth opportunities and maintain a disciplined approach to financial management. Now let's take a closer look at our FX exposure. Next slide please. Our treasury strategy continues to balance attractive returns with prudent balance sheet management. We use FX swaps selectively to benefit from favorable TL yields where market conditions support their use.

At quarter-end, 67% of our cash, excluding FX swaps, and 87% of our financial debt are -- were denominated in hard currencies. We also maintained substantial hard currency liquidity as a neutral hedge against our FX liabilities. Following the removal of tax advantages for money market funds and ongoing CapEx payments, we significantly scaled back our FX swap book activities starting in early Q4. Long-term hedging costs remain elevated at approximately 40% annually for instruments that do not introduce additional FX risk. With the Central Bank's managed exchange rate policy expected to remain broadly unchanged, we intend to maintain our net short FX position near its current level and continue to benefit from this approach.

At the end of the third quarter, our FX debt stood at USD 4.3 billion, compared with USD 2.4 billion in FX denominated financial assets. In addition, we had a derivative portfolio equivalent to USD 1.4 billion. Our net short FX position, therefore, stood at approximately USD 1.3 billion, comfortably within our medium-term target range of plus or minus USD 1.5 billion. With that, we conclude our prepared remarks. We are now ready to take questions. Thank you.

Creality Debuts mBox, A Kid-Operated AI 3D Printer, at $329

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

HOUSTON, Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Creality, a global leader in the 3D printing industry, today introduces mBox, an AI 3D printer designed specifically for kids. Featuring a 153 Ã 153 Ã 153 mm build volume, the kid-operated printer brings together kid-safe designs, simple printing operations, and accessible creative tools to help young makers turn their ideas into physical creations. Priced at $329, mBox is now available exclusively on TikTok Shop in the U.S. from November 9 to December 10.

mBox is built for families with children aged 6â16 who enjoy drawing, block building, model making, DIY projects or exploring technologies. It is particularly designed for young creators who want to go beyond just buying ready-made toys and instead turn their own imagination into tangible and personalized creations, whether through independent projects at home or hands-on activities in the company of parents. mBox is also ideal for STEAM learning spaces where educators seek to integrate safe and simple 3D printers into everyday classroom subjects, like science experiments, engineering design, and creative arts.

Developed specially for kids, mBox prioritizes safety in its product engineering. Its fully enclosed chamber keeps the nozzle and moving components behind an enclosure while children watch their creations take shape. During printing, the unheated build plate eliminates the need to handle a heated bed when removing finished prints, while activated carbon filtration helps filter impurities from the chamber air.

Notably, a configurable door-open alert offers three response options: no action, alert only, or alert and pause. When the alert-and-pause is set and triggered, printing stops and parents receive an app notification.

Together, these thoughtful design features help create a safe and friendly space for printing and creating, ensuring parents feel more at ease as children build 3D models on their own.

mBox focuses on simplified operations to make 3D printing easier for kids to get started with.

With the 3.97-inch full-color touchscreen, kids can pick a model and start printing in just a few clicks without connecting to a phone. Before printing, auto leveling simplifies print preparation and helps improve first-layer adhesion, reducing the need for parents' manual adjustments. During printing, the CoreXY motion system with vibration compensation supports stable printing and cleaner surface details, while AI detection uses the built-in camera to identify issues like warping, foreign objects, and spaghetti failures, and then alerts are sent to parents through the app.

In addition, there is RGB status lighting to show print progress and a low-noise mode which keeps operating noise at or under 46 dB.

Beyond the printer itself, mBox bridges kids with dedicated software, Creality Park App and Creality Park Studio. The Creality Park App is a 3D playground showcasing curated models and STEAM courses in a fun way and offering pick & print experience for younger users. For those ready to take their ideas further, the Creality Park Studio, a PC-based platform, offers approachable 3D modeling tools to help design original creations.

The ecosystem also incorporates AI tools CubeMe and SnapForm, enabling kids to turn photos into personalized, printable figurines, keychains, and accessories.

From a simple idea to a piece of creation, mBox aims to spark imagination and encourage hands-on making, helping young creators turn inspiration into something they can hold in hands.

mBox is now available exclusively on the U.S. TikTok Shop at the price of $329 from November 9 to December 10.

QC Inc (QUBT) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Management details the shift from research toward scalable, commercial manufacturing.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Quantum Computing Inc. (QUBT +8.37%) reported record quarterly revenue driven by the integration of acquired photonics and advanced packaging businesses. Management reported a strategic shift from research and development toward scalable manufacturing and commercial deployment, prioritizing the growth of its photonic and advanced packaging products. The company is focusing on integrating 11 facilities across eight states to support its quantum roadmap and improve operating efficiency. While the company maintains a substantial cash position of $1.3 billion, it remains focused on integrating recent acquisitions and scaling production to meet demand in aerospace, government, and industrial markets.

Operator: Good day, ladies and gentlemen. And welcome to the Quantum Computing Inc. Third Quarter 26 Shareholder Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. Following today's prepared remarks, the line will be open for questions. It is now my pleasure to introduce you to your host, David Moskowitz. Head of investor relations at QCI. David, please go ahead.

David Moskowitz: Thank you, operator, and welcome to QCI's third quarter 26 financial results and business update conference call. Before we begin, please note that today's remarks include forward looking statements including statements about our expected results, plans, strategy and market opportunities. These statements are based on current expectations and involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. These risks are described in today's press release and in our SEC filings including our most recent Forms 10-K and 10-Q. These statements speak only as of today, and we undertake no obligation to update them except as required by law. On the call today, we have Dr.

Yuping Huang, QCI's Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and Christopher Bruce Roberts, our CFO. The team will provide an update on the business followed by a question-and-answer session. I will now turn the call over to Yuping. Please go ahead.

Yuping Huang: Thank you, David. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Looking at our third quarter and the year so far, I believe QCI is entering an important new stage. We have spent years building photonic based quantum technology designed for the real world. Now we are beginning to see our investments come together and our attention is shifting from what we can build to what we can put to work for customers. That means getting our technologies into customers' hands. Delivering on our commitments and building a business that can grow sustainably. Execution matters. More than ever. Our third quarter results reflect progress in that direction.

In Q3, we generated a record revenue of $9.5 million led primarily by our expanded photonics business which serves customers across a range of established markets. The acquisitions completed this year added established products and customer relationships. As well as manufacturing capabilities, essential to our quantum road map. That gives us commercial opportunities to grow revenue today while supporting the technologies we are developing for the future. During the quarter, we provided cloud access to our Directory system to Hamed Khalifa University in Qatar. Supporting the research education and adoption of quantum computing and networking.

That builds early progress including the installation of a directory optimization system at a leading global consulting firm and the agreement with Planck Dynamics for our neural wave reservoir computer in defense applications. More recently, we announced our next generation Dirac-3 quantum optimization machine which is designed to solve optimization problems with up to 9.98 thousand variables, an important step. In our quantum computing road map. We expect the first customer shipment during the fourth quarter. As a part of the announcement, we published the benchmarking results involving problems with up to 9.98 thousand variables, comparing the system's performance with leading classical optimization solvers.

We are encouraged by these results and what they tell us about the progress in developing increasingly capable quantum systems. This is still work to do as we evaluate performance across different applications. But advances like these bring us closer to solving larger more complex problems for customers. These are encouraging developments for sure. But what matters most is what customers can ultimately do with our quantum technology. Our recently announced collaboration with ImmuBio is a good example. Our collaboration with ImmuBio is exploring how direct optimization AI and the conventional analytics could potentially identify new insights for clinical research data. It is early work, but it reflects what matters most to me.

That the true measure of innovation is not just what a technology can do, but what it enables others to achieve. that is exactly the thinking behind the broader platform we are building. Our quantum photonics platform, extends beyond computing into sensing and communications. as well. Some applications are commercial today while others need further development and validation. Our manufacturing capabilities connect these opportunities. By combining photonic design, chip manufacturing, and advanced packaging at our North Carolina facility and our thin film lithium niobate facility in Arizona. We gain greater control over development and production. This infrastructure serves 2 important purposes. Supporting our proprietary quantum systems and serving established photonics markets.

The task now is to integrate it effectively and deliver for customers. With that in mind, we are focused on 3 priorities over the next, 12 to 24 months. The first is growing our commercial business. We have an opportunity to build on the established businesses and customer relationships we have added. While expanding the market for our quantum and advanced photonics systems. Our photonics and advanced packaging businesses provide a commercial foundation we can grow today. While supporting the development of our quantum technologies. As those technologies mature, we see opportunities to introduce them to a broader range of customers.

Our goal is to turn growing interest in QCI into orders. a stronger backlog, deployments, and the lasting customer relationships. Second is to scale manufacturing. We are bringing operations together expanding capacity and improving efficiency. Reliable repeatable production matters as our quantum technologies mature. Our third priority is advancing our quantum portfolio. We have achieved all the objective outlined in our 24 to 26 portfolio road map. So we are moving into the new phase to scale our manufacturing and product lines. Our goal is to make quantum systems smaller more capable, and easier to deploy. A major part of that work involves integrating more of our technology onto photonics chips.

Which brings us closer to the compact practical systems we envision for the future. These 3 priorities are closely connected. Our quantum road map guides the technologies we develop our manufacturing capabilities, help us bring those technologies into production. And our commercial efforts helped us understand where customers see value and where we should focus our resources. It is how we move from building the technology to build a sustainable business around it. That brings me back to something fundamental about QSAR and why we have chosen photonics as our approach. I believe for many years, that light offers 1 of the most promising path to making quantum technology practical and accessible. There are several approaches to quantum computing.

As we all know, each with its own strength and challenges. We choose photonics because we believe it offers important advantages in bringing quantum technology into broad real world use. Our direct systems, for example, operate at room temperature, with relatively low power requirements and without the specialized cryogenic infrastructure. Required by many other approaches. That can make a meaningful difference in terms of cost. And the complexity. Photonics also allows us to build on decades of advances in optical technology and the semiconductor manufacturing. And with the capabilities we have assembled at QSI, we are bringing more of that process under our own control. This is still considerable work ahead.

But I believe this approach gives us a strong foundation for the future. My ambition has always been to make quantum technology useful and accessible on the much broader scale. And I believe Light offers a practical near term path toward that goal. When you are taking the journey 1 step at a time. And I am encouraged by the progress we have made. With our solid Q3 results as evidence. With that, I will turn the call over Christopher to review our third quarter financial results and how we are managing our resources to support the work ahead. Christopher?

Meta introduces Muse Ember to power cost-efficient AI agents

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Meta Platforms Inc. today introduced Muse Ember, an entry-level artificial intelligence model that costs significantly less than the competition.

Notably, it’s the first AI that the company trained using Muse Wonder. The latter algorithm is the Facebook parent’s flagship large language model. Meta didn’t specify which part of the workflow it automated with Muse Wonder.

One possibility is that the company used it to perform post-training, the task of honing a model’s capabilities by training it on additional data. Thinking Machines Labs Inc. recently demonstrated that even a relatively small LLM can run post-training runs end-to-end. Anthropic PBC, for its part, last week revealed that its AI models could soon gain the ability to significantly accelerate machine learning research.

Applications often use frontier LLMs such as Muse Wonder as part of AI ensembles. When a user enters a request, the frontier LLM splits it into smaller tasks and assigns them to agents powered by a lower-cost model. Meta says Muse Ember is specifically optimized to play the latter role.

The company evaluated the model using the Artificial Analysis Index, which aggregates nine AI benchmarks spanning use cases such as coding and financial analysis. Meta says that Muse Ember matched the score of Anthropic’s entry-level Claude Haiku 5.5 model at about a third the price. It also outperformed OpenAI Group PBC’s comparable GPT-6 Luna algorithm.

The same internal evaluation saw Meta test Muse Ember and the two rival models across nine other benchmarks. All three algorithms were in “max” mode, which means they used the maximum amount of hardware at their disposal instead of prioritizing cost-efficiency. Muse Ember outperformed Haiku and Luna across seven of the benchmarks.

The area where the model appears to have the biggest edge is business task automation. Whereas most of Muse Ember’s benchmark results were only a few percentage points better than those of Haiku and Luna, it clocked a 17% lead on AutomationBench-AA. It’s a collection of 657 tasks that span popular cloud applications such as Gmail and Salesforce.

Muse Ember has a context window of 1 million tokens, which enables it to ingest lengthy business documents. Users can also include images, audio and video in their prompts. The model generates responses up to 512,000 tokens in length.

Muse Ember is available through Meta’s Model API for 10 cents per million input tokens and 50 cents per million output tokens. A built-in cache can reuse frequently used prompts to avoid duplicate processing. When the feature is active, Muse Ember’s pricing drops to 0.4 cents per million input tokens.

We're well past Big Brother Season 28's finale on the 2026 TV schedule, but former Houseguests are still taking shots at each other. Runner-up Taylor Brown has had a chance to watch some episodes, and as a result, she was able to see what Melody Morris had to say. With that, Taylor is now wondering how Melody had any right to discuss strategy.

In a recent livestream featuring fellow Houseguest LaTrice "LaLa" Verrett and one of BB's most memorable winners, Jun Song, Taylor went off. Brown mentioned Melody's critique against her and how she supported the narrative that the latter "did nothing" in the game. On top of all that, Taylor also wanted to know what made Melody any different:

What do you do? I would say we're the same person, different fonts! Because if you asked me, anytime I was in the pod I looked in the mirror and you were under me! She was in the bed just as much as me...if the perception is just I'm cooking and cleaning, what are you doing?

She makes a good point, but it's also one that many other Big Brother fans have been making. Those outside the house were equally frustrated that Melody hadn't done anything in the game, even when her closest allies were in jeopardy. Meanwhile, she was hanging out with members of F.A.P. and The Crossovers and talking about how Taylor did nothing in the game.

Dee's Advice For Future Big Brother Houseguests Is Exactly What The Series Needs

As for why Taylor is only bringing this up now, it always takes a while for Big Brother's late-game Houseguests to catch up with what others were saying during the season. They obviously couldn't watch the live feeds with a Paramount+ subscription, and sometimes the television edit is deceiving.

Given that, I think Taylor has finally had the time to check out some of the episodes and see some of the live feed clips sent to her by fans. This probably prompted the response about Melody, who truly didn't have a better chance of winning Big Brother than Taylor did, in my opinion.

When talking about her own game, Taylor has acknowledged her shortcomings. She admitted that the finale Q&A was not her finest moment and that she choked when it came to answering the big questions. She also called out Angela Murray and others for their reactions to her questions, which Melody also played a part in.

As for Melody, she hasn't mentioned Taylor a that much in the past few weeks. Primarily, she's been on a tour around the United States with Drew Campbell, and simultaneously continues to tease fans about whether or not they're dating. I would be curious to see what Melody has to say about all of this, and if there's any mutual beef on her end with Taylor putting her on blast.

Big Brother Season 28 is available to stream over on Paramount+. With the post-season drama still going on between Houseguests, it may be worth a rewatch just to get refreshed on all that went down, because even I'm struggling to remember how these feuds started.

Every senior with an Apple Watch should set up these 5 health alerts

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

From emergency help to medication reminders, your Apple Watch can support you as you age.

Apple Watches are owned by people of all ages, so wearing one doesn't mark you as vulnerable, unlike a medical pendant. This is important to some older people who do not see themselves as "seniors", as explained by the National Institute of Aging. Older individuals know age does not stop them from living independent lives, and an Apple Watch can help them stay healthy when they do.

The idea that technology can help older people live independently for longer is hugely attractive to independent-minded boomers. Stand and movement reminders, fitness tracking and the step counter help seniors stay more active, keeping them healthier for longer. As Apple invests in healthcare research, the smartwatch gets better at detecting short term illness, boosting self-care.

With permission, the Find My app helps younger people take better care of their elderly relatives by tracking their location. There are also a number of health alerts every senior with an Apple Watch should set up.

Apple Watch has great tools for emergency help, which can be especially beneficial for seniors. These include Emergency SOS, Medical ID and Emergency Contacts.

Emergency SOS contacts emergency services when things go wrong. To use this feature, press and hold the side button, then drag the Emergency Call slider or keep holding the button until the call is made. This needs a cellular watch with an active plan, Wi-Fi calling or the paired iPhone nearby.

To turn on Emergency SOS, open the Watch app on your iPhone, tap Emergency SOS and turn on Hold Side Button to Dial.

Access to Medical ID and Emergency Contacts can be found in the Health app on your iPhone. Tap your profile picture and select Medical ID. Tap Edit, enter your details and add trusted Emergency Contacts. Medics who find your Apple Watch will review your Medical ID, so keep your allergies or conditions up to date to help medics deliver the treatment you need.

Over one in four people aged 65 or older fall unexpectedly each year, says the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). In addition, 319,000 older people are hospitalized for hip fractures after a fall every year. Pew Research claims that, in 2023, 26% of US adults aged 65 or older lived alone, which compounds the potential risk of falling. Fall Detection may protect them.

Fall Detection is enabled automatically if you tell the Health app you are 55 or older. Once activated, it will call emergency services if the built-in sensors on your Apple Watch detect you are immobile after taking a fall.

If you fall, an alert message appears on your Apple Watch display, asking if you fell. If you request help, do not answer or remain immobile, the system will call emergency services. To turn on Fall Detection, open Emergency SOS on your iPhone and toggle feature On. On Apple Watch, open Settings > SOS, toggle Fall Detection to On, Select Always On and confirm.

Crash Detection does the same after a car crash and is available on recent Apple Watch models. To turn on Crash Detection, go to Emergency SOS and toggle Call After Serious Crash to On.

CDC data shows that a person dies of cardiovascular disease every 34 seconds in the US. While an Apple Watch cannot identify heart attacks, it can help monitor overall heart health including continuous heart rate monitoring and help to identify atrial fibrillation.

An Apple Watch uses green and infrared LED lights on its back to continuously measure your heart rate. This feature works automatically. Another feature lets you take an accurate ECG (electrocardiogram) reading to help detect irregular heart rates or the signs of atrial fibrillation. To use the ECG, open the ECG app, hold your wrist steady and touch the Digital Crown with your finger — you'll get a reading in thirty seconds.

The watch will also warn you if your heart goes above or below set thresholds, such as above 120bpm or below 40bpm. Apple Watch shares this information with the Health app on your iPhone, where you will find a VO2 Max reading that assesses your overall cardio fitness based on the information gathered by the sensors on your watch.

To enable Heart-related features on your Apple Watch, open Settings > Heart and toggle the available heart features you want to use On.

Forget to take your pills? Medication Reminders can help you stay up-to-date. To set this up, open the Health app on your iPhone, tap Browse > Medications and then Add Medication. Search for your medicine, tap Add, follow the prompts for setting up a schedule and tap Done.

You can add multiple medications, after which your Apple Watch will tap your wrist and send you a notification when it's time to take your dose. You can create a log of medicinal compliance to share with a doctor. Bonus: The sleep tracker on Apple Watch can flag potential sleep apnea for medical investigation. To set it up, open Sleep on Apple Watch (or in the Health app on your iPhone). Turn on Track Sleep with Apple Watch. In the Health app, tap Browse > Respiratory > Sleep Apnea Notifications.

Apple believes everyone should be able to use its technology and includes accessibility features in its products for no extra charge. That commitment extends to the Apple Watch, which is packed with tools to help people live independent lives.

Hearing loss becomes more common with age, with Achieve claiming one in four US adults in their sixties suffer from it. Apple's Sound Recognition tool helps by using the Apple Watch and iPhone to listen for specific sounds, such as doorbells, sirens or fire alarms.

Enable Sound Recognition in Accessibility Settings on your iPhone. Tap Sound & Name Recognition > Sound Recognition, toggle to On and choose the sounds you want it to recognize.

Apple has also figured out how to make Apple Watch more usable by those who are visually impaired. Press the side button to open Control Center, tap the AA icon and turn the Digital Crown to adjust font size to make it easier to read. If you want more information on any of these features, Apple provides an extensive explanation here.

In the run-up to the COP31 U.N. climate change conference, scientists have revealed that global carbon emissions from fossil fuels are projected to drop by 0.4% this year, driven by growth in installed wind and solar power capacity, as well as oil price hikes caused by the Iran conflict. But climate goals are still unlikely to be met.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The world's carbon emissions from oil, gas and coal are projected to decrease by 0.4% this year, driven partly by the expansion of solar and wind power capacity and the price increases caused by the Iran conflict, according to a new report.

The 2026 Global Carbon Budget report was published in the journal Earth System Science Data Nov. 10 and is due to be presented at the U.N. Climate Change Conference's COP31 meeting in Antalya, Turkey, this week.

Global carbon emissions have increased steadily since record-keeping began. This year is projected to have a slight decrease in fossil-fuel emissions, but that is partly due to price increases caused by the Iran conflict.

It is the first time annual carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from fossil fuels have fallen since the coronavirus pandemic in 2020. But the overall emissions picture suggests the world is still likely to miss key climate goals.

"It is an encouraging sign that the growth of emissions is slowing and decarbonisation efforts are starting to make a difference," said Joeri Rogelj, a climate scientist at the Centre for Environmental Policy at Imperial College London who wasn't involved in the research. "However, at 0.4%, the projected decline is very small," Rogelj told Live Science in an email.

The report projects 38.2 billion metric tons (42.1 billion U.S. tons) of emissions of the climate-warming greenhouse gas CO2 from fossil fuel sources this year. Greenhouse gases trap heat by absorbing the sun's radiation, and as their concentrations in the atmosphere increase, so do global average temperatures, leading to altered weather patterns and higher sea levels, as well as other major impacts.

The war with Iran has resulted in restricted fuel availability and high prices, with a corresponding reduction in demand

Part of the 0.4% reduction in CO2 emissions is attributable to 40 countries that have cut emissions over the past decade while growing their economies. These include the U.S., Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, the United Kingdom, Japan and about 30 countries in the European Union, the researchers reported.

When it comes to some of the biggest emitters, annual CO2 emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9% in China, 1.3% in the U.S., 1.5% in the European Union and 1% in Japan, but India's annual CO2 emissions are projected to grow by 4.4%.

Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

Carbon emissions are projected to decrease slightly in the U.S., China and the E.U. but to increase in India.

Fossil-fuel-linked CO2 emissions from the rest of the world are projected to decrease by 0.7%, driven mainly by a 1.9% drop in oil emissions. The report authors suggested that this is a short-term response to the global supply constraints and increased prices triggered by the Iran conflict.

"The war with Iran has resulted in restricted fuel availability and high prices, with a corresponding reduction in demand," Rogelj said.

While fossil fuel emissions and demand for oil are declining globally, overall demand for energy is actually increasing.

"Based only on the demand for energy, which has grown, we would have expected an increase in fossil CO2 emissions by about 0.8 gigatonnes," said study co-author Judith Hauck, a biogeoscientist at the Alfred Wegener Institute, Helmholtz Centre for Polar and Marine Research in Germany.

About two-thirds of that increase in demand is being met by solar and wind power and electric vehicles, showing that clean technologies are making a real difference in reducing global emissions, Hauck said. However, the hike in energy prices that resulted from the Iran conflict also decreased demand by 0.4%, she said.

"So only together with the energy crisis did we bring the change in emissions down to negative," Hauck told Live Science, adding that she expects CO2 emissions to rebound if the conflict ends, as they did after the temporary emissions drop caused by the lockdowns during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The exceptional circumstances that energy markets experienced this year make it clear that the small projected emissions decline is no reason to declare that emissions are now reducing, but there are hopeful signs, Rogelj said.

"Despite my muted enthusiasm about whether these lower emissions for 2026 represent the start of a long-term decline, the analysis shows encouraging signs of deeper long-term structural changes," he said. "But this shift must accelerate to ensure it is not outpaced by energy demand growth."

The report found that clean energy growth isn't yet fast enough to drive a steady decline in global CO2 emissions attributable to fossil fuels. The study authors expect that to happen in the next few years, Hauck said, as long as there is a continued push to deploy solar and wind power, batteries and electric vehicles.

CO2 emissions from fossil fuels are just part of the picture, though. Because of increases in human-caused peat fires, deforestation and forest fires linked to dry El Niño conditions, total global CO2 emissions from all sources this year are projected to increase slightly from 42.8 billion metric tons (47.2 billion U.S. tons) last year to reach a record 43.3 billion metric tons (47.7 billion U.S. tons) this year, according to the report.

This means that the total budget of CO2 that can be emitted before global warming reaches 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above preindustrial levels is now just 150 billion metric tons (165 billion U.S. tons) ‪—‬ equivalent to less than four years of emissions at the current rate.

Hauck, like many climate scientists, thinks we have already missed our chance to hit the 1.5 C target and could only get back to that level through extensive removal of CO2 from the atmosphere.?

"I'm still hopeful for something between 1.5 and 2 C [3.6 F]," Hauck said. "But for 1.5 degrees, we would need to see such a drastic strong drop in emissions. Based on what we've seen in the past years, even with this strong increase in avoided emissions, I don't think we can make that."

To halt global warming from increasing ever further, the world needs to be more ambitious in its planned emissions cuts, said Rogeli. We need to bring annual emissions down to zero to protect future generations from a double whammy of “having to try to transform economies so that they produce less climate pollution, while dealing with the impacts and damages of an increasingly adverse climate system," he said.

Chris Simms is a freelance journalist who previously worked at New Scientist for more than 10 years, in roles including chief subeditor and assistant news editor. He was also a senior subeditor at Nature and has a degree in zoology from Queen Mary University of London. In recent years, he has written numerous articles for New Scientist and in 2018 was shortlisted for Best Newcomer at the Association of British Science Writers awards.

AI-Powered Precision Brain Stimulation Reduces PTSD in Weeks

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

After years or decades, problems and patterns can become deeply entrenched. Be a fly on the wall during a sample couples therapy session and witness the slow, deliberate work of changing those patterns for a more enduring love.

Self Tests are all about you. Are you outgoing or introverted? Are you a narcissist? Does perfectionism hold you back? Find out the answers to these questions and more with Psychology Today.

Posted November 9, 2026 | Reviewed by Davia Sills

Neuroscience is at the start of a tsunami of innovation thanks to artificial intelligence (AI). Machine learning can identify meaningful biological indicators from reams of noisy brain activity data to offer more personalized, targeted treatment. A new study in the November-December 2026 edition of Personalized Medicine in Psychiatry shows how the combination of AI with noninvasive transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) can reduce post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in just two weeks.

“These findings mark a significant step forward in PTSD therapy, offering a non-pharmacologic treatment for individuals who have not benefited from traditional therapeutic approaches,” wrote the research team of Alexander Taghva, Jeffery Lindquist, and Anthony Kim.

An estimated 70 percent of the world’s population will experience a traumatic event during their lifetime, yet only 5.6 percent will develop post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) from the experience, according to the World Health Organization. In the U.S. alone, an estimated 7.7 million adult Americans suffer from PTSD, according to the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH).

Post-traumatic stress disorder is a mental health condition where symptoms may emerge for up to three months after a stressful or traumatic event, persist for more than a month, and interfere with performing daily life activities.

Adults with PTSD have at least one symptom of re-experiencing and avoidance, in addition to at least two symptoms related to problems with arousal and reactivity, as well as cognition and mood issues, per NIMH. Symptoms of re-experiencing may include flashbacks, physical signs of stress, distressing thoughts, and recurring memories or dreams. Evading feelings or thoughts associated with the trauma, or staying away from anything that might be a reminder of the traumatic event, are symptoms of avoidance. Issues with arousal and reactivity may include irritability, outbursts, risky behavior, insomnia, concentration problems, tenseness, or skittishness. PTSD symptoms that affect cognition and mood include difficulty feeling positive, feeling socially isolated, loss of interest in normal activities, persistent negative thoughts and emotions, exaggerated feelings of blame, and trouble recalling crucial elements of traumatic events.

Factors that may increase the potential for PTSD include prior traumatic experiences, especially childhood trauma, a history of mental illness or mental illness in the family, post-event stressors such as the death of a loved one, injury, or job loss, lack of social support post-trauma, and feelings of extreme fear, helplessness, or horror, according to the National Institute of Mental Health.

PTSD treatment options include psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), cognitive processing therapy (CPT), prolonged exposure, eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy, narrative exposure therapy (NET), and medications, according to the American Psychological Association (APA). Common PTSD antidepressants, per the APA, include the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) sertraline (generic name for Zoloft), paroxetine (generic name for Paxil), and fluoxetine (generic name for Prozac), and serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) like venlafaxine (generic name for Effexor).

“The results of this study are particularly meaningful in the context of PTSD treatment, where a substantial fraction of patients does not fully respond to existing pharmacologic and psychological therapies,” wrote the study authors.

For this study, the researchers focused on PTSD among the veterans. The study participants included over 70 military veterans between the ages of 18 and 55 years who were diagnosed with PTSD, of whom 36 were randomly selected to receive non-invasive brain stimulation treatment and 37 received placebo treatment.

“The prevalence of combat-related PTSD among U.S. military veterans is estimated to be 7 percent, with prevalence increased among female service members (13 percent) in comparison to males (6 percent),” the researchers wrote.

First, a baseline electroencephalogram (EEG) was recorded noninvasively via a sensor cap for 10 minutes at the same time as an electrocardiogram (EKG). The treatment frequency was determined via an AI decision tree algorithm output based on the 10-minute EEG data recordings as input. Recordings were done at the start and end of the therapy. For a period of two weeks, study participants received 10 real or placebo treatments. Those receiving the actual treatment received personalized neuromodulation, where repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) was customized to the participant’s resting-state EEG alpha rhythm.

Brain waves are patterns of neuronal electrical activity that are a continuous series of peaks and troughs that occur between neurons via electrical pulses and are measured in Hertz (Hz). EEG measures brain waves via their electrical activity. Depending on the frequencies and amplitude, brain waves are categorized as alpha (8-12 Hz), beta (13-30 Hz), theta (4-10 Hz), delta (0.5-1.5 Hz), or gamma (30-120 Hz) oscillations.

In 1924, German psychiatrist Hans Berger (1873-1941) was the first to record human electrical brain signals using EEG. Berger observed a 10-cycles-per-second rhythm and named it “alpha.”

Alpha brain waves happen during a state of calmness and relaxation that occurs when meditating lightly, sitting quietly with eyes closed, or daydreaming.

In this study, the researchers personalized the repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) pulse rate to the individual participant’s resting-state EEG alpha (α) rhythm, a process called alpha repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (α-rTMS). The brain stimulation device used for the study was the FDA-cleared EEG-guided neuromodulation device for adults with PTSD called MeRT by Wave Neuroscience, based in Newport Beach, California.

The research team reported a 34 percent reduction in PTSD symptom severity and better sleep, with a 44 percent reduction in sleep disturbances as measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index Addendum for PTSD (PSQI-A), which measures sleep problems in PTSD patients.

“The effectiveness of ⍺-rTMS could be attributed to its precision in targeting dysregulated alpha band activity, possibly related to the underlying default mode network (DMN), implicated in PTSD’s neuropathology,” the researchers posited. “This precision heralds a novel, more personalized approach to neuromodulation therapies, potentially increasing efficacy, to effectively address certain PTSD-related symptoms.”

Humble Hauler autonomous trailer takes the truck out of trucking [update]

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Less than a year after its founding, truckless trucking brand Humble Robotics has secured more than $75 million after a $51 million Series A funding round that will fuel the company’s transition from prototype to preproduction.

The latest funding round for the driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform developer was led by Obvious Ventures with participation from other existing investors Eclipse and Energy Impact Partners. Humble said it will use the funding for customer pilots, testing and validation, and early manufacturing.

“We’ve spent years proving that a truck can drive itself,” explains Humble Robotics founder and CEO, Eyal Cohen. “The harder question is how to make autonomy something a freight operator can depend on every day.”

We originally covered the Humble Hauler back in May. You can check out the original article, below, then let us know what you think of the company’s prospects in the comments.

The startup that dares to ask, “Why does the Macbook driving my freight around need a whole cab?” just showed off a fully driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform designed to handle containerized cargo more efficiently than ever.

Instead of looking at the tractor and asking how to make it work without a driver, Humble looked at the trailer, itself, redesigning the container chassis as a vehicle from the ground up. The end result isn’t just an autonomous solution, it’s an overall lighter platform without a cab that saves shippers the weight of a sleeper cab, a day cab, or the truck at all.

The Humble approach is said to improve payload efficiency of shipping containers, and intended for dock-to-dock operation.

“I have dedicated my career to building electric and autonomous vehicle technology,” explains Eyal Cohen, Humble Robotics’ founder and CEO. “For the first time, freight can be fully automated all the way to the loading dock. We are making freight sustainable, safe and efficient in a way no one thought was possible. And we’re doing it with an exceptional team of industry veterans and AV experts.”

Emerging from stealth after a $24 million funding round, Humble claims to have completed its first Humble Hauler prototype in less than six months – and they’ll soon be ready to begin autonomous testing in pilot programs with a number of logistics partners.

The vehicle uses a combination of cameras, lidar, and radar for 360-degree awareness (unhindered by seeing around a cab), and uses vision-language-action models to help the system respond to new scenarios.

Thanks to superior battery tech, a maturing global charging infrastructure, and a permanently damaged MidEast oil supply, there’s never been a better time to be an EV startup. Humble is hitting all the electric trailer buzzwords, too, while also touting the fact that the electric powertrain can reduce a company’s to volatile fuel prices even as it helps produce other cost benefits like lower maintenance costs.

There is a reason why the transportation industry developed separate cabs and trailers. Trailers can be loaded or unloaded for days and are much less expensive than trucks that serve both purposes in one piece. That allows the more expensive piece of the transport puzzle to be used more and allows the trailer to be loaded and unloaded while the cab is elsewhere working or in the shop. Query whether the savings they cite will surpass the costs of not having the flexibility of a cab and trailer design.

And if a robot like this can deliver on its promises without the baked-in inefficiencies of humanoids, they might be one step closer to provide that the most efficient solution to a problem is rarely a general one, and even rarer is it a solution that looks like a human.

Viant Buys Waymark For $20 Million, Because CTV Needs More Ads (More!)

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Viant had a pretty good third quarter. The open internet apparently had nothing to do with it, though.

On Monday evening, the company reported just over $110 million in revenue for Q3, up 29% year over year. CTV ad spend increased almost 40% over the same time period, representing more than half of the total ad spend through Viant’s platform.

Viant also used its earnings call to announce the close of its acquisition of AI video creative production platform Waymark for $20 million in cash, a deal designed to help advertisers make more CTV ads faster.

Despite the news, Viant’s stock was down around 7% in after-hours trading. It’s not immediately clear why, but spending could be a factor. Viant expects its costs to rise about 25% next quarter, partly because of acquisitions like TVision and Waymark that aren’t expected to bring in meaningful revenue yet.

But hey, maybe that’s just the price of going all in on CTV, and Viant isn’t hedging.

Tim Vanderhook, Viant’s CEO, hyped Waymark as the start of an “era of generative ad creative for CTV” and said it could attract thousands if not millions of new advertisers to connected TV.

But where does that leave the open web? In the corner with no Patrick Swayze to save it.

During the Q&A portion of the call, Laura Martin, an analyst at Needham & Company, asked how Viant plans to keep growing revenue when the open internet is starting to shrivel like a slug in salt and even its longstanding champions, like Reddit, are throwing in the towel.

In response, Tim Vanderhook said that the open internet is only “10% or less” of Viant’s business and is “certainly not driving the growth rates we’re seeing now.”

As far as Viant is concerned, every dollar leaving the open web is a dollar headed toward CTV.

Advertisers are shifting more of their budgets away from display and online video towards more addressable and “premium” environments, Vanderhook said, which he believes will “end up being a catalyst for us next year.”

Still, just because budgets are moving to CTV, doesn’t mean every advertiser can afford to make a TV ad – and that’s where Waymark comes in.

Waymark’s software turns a brand’s inputs into a finished video ad in a matter of minutes, complete with a custom script, visuals and voiceover. Local media sellers, including Spectrum Reach, Comcast, NBCU and Fox already use it to produce linear and CTV spots for local advertisers.

In Viant’s view, Waymark addresses three problems: the high cost of producing TV-quality ads, creative fatigue and ads that aren’t tailored to the audience.

Production costs keep most small and midsize advertisers out of CTV, said Viant’s COO, Chris Vanderhook, and so “the down market opportunity is incredible.”

But big enterprise advertisers also need more creative. They run the same ads over and over again until people just tune them out, Tim Vanderhook said.

“It’s not that the creative is bad,” he said, “it’s that they do a big production shoot, they have that creative in market for three to six months and users are overfrequented.”

Viant’s TVision panel data suggests that when someone has seen an ad too many times, their attention plummets, but fresh creative can increase their attention by more than 80%.

The final part of the equation is targeting. Viant plans to pair Waymark with its Household ID, Iris Content ID and TVision’s attention data to tailor different creative versions to specific audiences and also to what they’re watching.

Take an online university that’s trying to reach prospective students. Instead of running a single ad for everyone, the advertiser could have one about athletics, another about academics, a third about campus life and so on.

Viant would use its Household ID to match an ad to the right audience (sports fans, say, or academically minded prospects). The content ID would contextually target the ad to whatever’s on the screen (the athletics ad during a sports game and the academic ad during an ad break in a documentary). And then TVision could measure attention.

Chris Vanderhook referred to this process as “the transformation of creative from a fixed asset into a dynamic asset.”

Even so, for now at least, Waymark is more of a bet than a business. Viant expects it to add little revenue this quarter or next year. But the deal does fit the pattern. Viant is going for those CTV dollars.

“The paradigm is shifting,” Tim Vanderhook said. “TV is no longer reserved only for the world’s largest brands.”

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Before the Arrowverse existed, fans had a Superman show without Superman called Smallville, and that series defined my childhood. Now, it’s celebrating it’s 25th anniversary (and making me feel old). The series focuses squarely on Clark Kent, and it makes some interesting choices regarding the DC mythos. Interestingly, the show never saw Tom Welling's Clark fully suited up as the Man of Steel, and the actor himself shared some BTS details about why that was the case.

Just to refresh fans' memories, Clark never wore the classic red-and-blue suit, and barely hit the skies. However, the final moment gave a little wink at who this fan-favorite Clark Kent had become by showing him running across the rooftop of the Daily Planet and ripping open his shirt to reveal the classic S on the chest. This was the closest fans came to seeing the actor in the hero tights.

When Welling and his co-star, Michael Rosenbaum, (who played Lex Luther) spoke with Variety, he revealed the reason behind the lack of a super suit:

We got to set that day, and they had given me just a T-shirt with no sleeves to wear underneath the shirt. Because they didn’t have the money to put the suit on, and they weren’t going to see it anyway.

The absence of a full suit wasn’t a major surprise, given creators Alfred Gough and Miles Millar initiated a “no flights, no tights” rule when they started the show. Only one of those was ever broken. While Welling admits that they “toed the line a few times” when it came to the suit, they never did get the actor in a pair of tights. The reason for that was pretty simple. They weren’t able to do so unless Welling gave the “all right,” and to this day, this iteration of Clark has not suited up.

Funny enough, the closest we came to seeing Clark in a hero costume was when he wore the Green Arrow suit for an episode. Years later, along with Erica Durance (who played Lois Lane), Welling did reprise his role as Clark for a scene in the Arrowverse's "Crisis on Infinite Earths” crossover event, though even by that point, the character had given up his powers and retired as a hero. Despite Kent not taking to the skies in the final shot, Welling enjoyed the series, and he had this to say about his character's status:

We can’t go with him. But he’s out there.

This is technically true, and there have also been plenty of Supermen before and after Smallville. Yet fans have remained dedicated to the series. That's partially thanks to Welling, Rosenbaum, and several cast members reuniting conventions around the country. Plus, Rosenbaum and Welling host the re-watch podcast “Talkville,” which is currently recapping Season 9. With that, fans continue to hear BTS stories and re-live their favorite moments.

While there have been other Supes shows, the former WB/CW series still stands as the only series to solely focus on Clark and not his alter ego. But this could change if Welling and Rosenbaum succeed in reviving the series. The duo have been reportedly attempting to bring back Smallville via an animated sequel, and this could potentially mean (finally) seeing Clark in the suit.

I'd still actually like to see Tom Welling don the costume in a live-action production, though, even if the chances of that happening seem slim to none. At the very least, fans can enjoy Clark's entire journey by streaming all 10 seasons of Smallville with a Hulu subscription.

LG Energy Solution Wins CES Innovation Awards 2027 for Its Fast and Precise Second-Life Battery Diagnostic System

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Energy Solution (KRX: 373220) today announced that Re.Pulse, its software-based state-of-health (SoH) diagnostic solution for used batteries, has been named an honoree in the Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility category at the CES Innovation AwardsÂ® 2027.

Reflecting its name, Re.Pulse embodies the concept of reviving the "pulse" of a used battery and giving it a second life. By applying current pulses and analyzing the resulting voltage response, the solution rapidly evaluates the SoH of a battery, whether in service or after removal. Based on the diagnostic results, used batteries can be directed to the most appropriate next step across three pathways: reuse, remanufacturing, or recycling, helping maximize their value throughout the battery lifecycle.

Re.Pulse addresses two key limitations of conventional battery diagnosis: lengthy testing times and the inability to identify localized degradation within a battery pack. While conventional SoH testing requires a full discharge-recharge-discharge cycle lasting more than seven hours, Re.Pulse estimates battery condition in under 10 minutes. It also advances diagnosis beyond conventional pack-level monitoring by evaluating SoH at the cell level, helping detect degraded cells that traditional methods cannot identify. Access to this more precise data enables users to take targeted action, such as repairing or replacing specific units, reducing the premature disposal of usable batteries as well as the carbon emissions associated with producing replacement batteries.

Re.Pulse is a software-based system that seamlessly integrates with standard battery capacity testers and EV chargers, eliminating the need for any additional dedicated hardware while enabling deployment across diverse environments such as EV maintenance and inspection centers, fleet operations, used-battery energy storage projects, and used-vehicle sales and evaluation platforms.

Diagnostic results will be provided across various formats, including web and mobile applications, allowing users to precisely determine battery SoH and make confident, informed decisions on the optimal pathway.

"The CES Innovation Award recognition demonstrates how our deep battery expertise can be combined with software innovation to create new value across the battery lifecycle," said Sanghoon Lee, leader of the Pack/BMS Research Service Solution Department at LG Energy Solution. "Through Re.Pulse, we aim to unlock greater value from used batteries by enabling more informed second-life decisions, while helping build a more sustainable and circular battery ecosystem."

As electrification expands across various sectors, accurate evaluation of batteries after their first use is becoming increasingly important to the economics and sustainability of the battery value chain. LG Energy Solution plans to continue advancing battery lifecycle management technologies and strengthening its Battery-as-a-Service capabilities across diagnostics, management, and second-life applications.

LG Energy Solution (KRX: 373220) is a leading global manufacturer of lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles, mobility, IT, and energy storage systems. With more than 30 years of experience in revolutionary battery technology and extensive research and development (R&D), the company is the top battery-related patent holder in the world with over 100,000 patents. Its robust global network, which spans North America, Europe, and Asia, includes battery manufacturing facilities established through joint ventures with major automakers. Committed to building a sustainable battery ecosystem, LG Energy Solution aims to achieve carbon neutrality across its value chain by 2050, while embodying the value of shared growth and promoting a diverse and inclusive corporate culture. To learn more about LG Energy Solution's ideas and innovations, visit https://news.lgensol.com.

James Gunn’s DC Studios Exit Came at the Worst Time

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

The news that James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-heads of DC Studios was a major shock, whether you're a longtime comic book fan or someone who's been enjoying the current slate of DC-themed projects. It also felt out of nowhere: while DC Studios had a bit of a road bump due to Supergirl's less-than-stellar reception, it more than made up for it with two critically acclaimed projects in Lanterns and Clayface. This decision will loom over future DC projects, and it comes at the wrong time.

While Gunn has taken to social media to stress that stepping down as co-CEO was his decision, eyebrows are being raised at the man chosen to replace him and Safran. Skydance has tapped Jeremy Latcham as DC Studios' new president and chief creative officer, and Latcham isn't lacking in terms of box office credits; he produced some of Marvel Studios' biggest movies, including The Avengers and Guardians of the Galaxy (which Gunn directed) alongside the highly underrated Dungeons and Dragons: Honor Among Thieves. Latcham's Marvel work likely led to his top spot at DC Studios, but it also highlights a recurring trend in DC-based movies.

Jeremy Latcham's hiring is far from the first time that Warner Bros. has hired a creative best known for working at Marvel Studios. Back in 2017, Joss Whedon was hired to complete principal photography on Justice League after Zack Snyder departed the project following the loss of his daughter, Autumn. The result was a disaster; Snyder's more operatic filmmaking style clashed with Whedon's zippy, quippy approach to writing superheroes. Add in accusations of "gross misconduct" by star Ray Fisher, and Whedon's time on Justice League ended rather poorly. It also meant that DC's bid to reclaim some of the Marvel magic was dead in the water.

Though it's never been said out loud, some fans have speculated that a large part of the reason Gunn was chosen as DC Studios' CEO, beyond his work on The Suicide Squad and Peacemaker, is his previous work on the Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy. However, Gunn proved that he could make DC Studios its own thing by delivering character-driven stories, whether it's the blood-soaked chaos of Creature Commandos or the sci-fi spectacle of Superman. Latcham needs to keep that in mind, rather than chasing Marvel Studios' success.

Four teams, four completely different reasons to put yourself in danger for strangers. This is the roster you actually belong on, what they would want from you, and what it would cost you to stay.

You belong where the stakes are largest and the personalities are loudest. This is a team of people who are all used to being the most important person in the room, which is exactly why it works and exactly why it keeps nearly falling apart.

You have never had the luxury of being thanked for this. The X-Men protect a world that has never once been comfortable with them existing, and something in you understands exactly why they keep doing it anyway.

You do not want colleagues, you want your people. The Titans are the team where the friendship came first and the world-saving turned up afterwards as an inconvenient side effect.

You are not asking who to trust. You worked out the answer a while ago and it was nobody in a cape. This is where you go once you have decided the people in charge need watching, and that nobody else is going to do it.

James Gunn and Peter Safran's departures come as DC Studios prepares to release its biggest movie yet, Man of Tomorrow. Written and directed by Gunn, Man of Tomorrow will feature Clark Kent (David Corenswet) and Lex Luthor (Nicholas Hoult) joining forces to battle the malevolent artificial intelligence, Brainiac (Lars Eidinger). It's also shaping up to be the massive event movie fans have been waiting for, with the cast now including Milly Alcock as Supergirl, Aaron Pierre as John Stewart, and even Xolo Maridueña as Blue Beetle. Next are Season 2 of Creature Commandos and The People vs. Gorilla Grodd, with future projects stillup in the air.

It raises the question: What direction will DC Studios take next? Both Gunn and Safran are shifting back into creative roles, with Gunn saying that he's written another movie post-Man of Tomorrow:

"That's not to say Peter and I are immediately done with DC or superheroes. We have Man of Tomorrow out this summer. And we've just been engaged on another DC project which I'm writing, and we'll see where it goes after that. And, of course, the characters we've set up will live on."

The opening credits for Superman mentioned that it was ushering in "a new era of Gods and Monsters," hinting at James Gunn and Peter Safran's plans for the DC Universe. Time will tell if those plans shake out under Jeremy Latcham's leadership.

Man of Tomorrow premieres in theaters on July 9, 2027.

Fossil fuel emissions are down in 2026. Green energy isn’t the reason

📅 Nov 09, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Every print subscription comes with full digital access

The decrease is probably temporary and a result of high gas prices from the Iran war

The disruption of oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Iran has raised oil and gas prices around the world. According to new projections, those higher fuel prices will decrease global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel burning in 2026 by about 0.16 gigatons from 2025.

Scientists project that global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels will decrease by 0.4 percent this year, after having grown by 0.8 percent each year on average from 2019 to 2025.

But the dip may not last. The lower emissions are probably driven by high oil prices stemming from the Iran war, researchers report November 9 in Nature Climate Change.

Global emissions probably would have grown again this year without the energy shock of the Iran war, says Glen Peters, a climate scientist at the Center for International Climate Research in Oslo, Norway. “So the energy transition that’s happening … it’s not quite big enough to get emissions heading downward yet.”

We summarize the week's scientific breakthroughs every Thursday.

For the study, Peters and his colleagues used data on countries’ electric vehicle stocks and wind and solar energy generation to project those technologies impacts on global fossil CO2 emissions through 2028. The team used the generative AI model Claude to source data and write code for analysis.

By year’s end, global emissions will reach 38.24 gigatons, the researchers found, which is about 0.16 gigatons less than were emitted in 2025. For comparison, annual global emissions fell by nearly two gigatons in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic and by about 0.5 gigatons in 2009 because of the global financial crisis.

If electric vehicle sales and solar and wind capacity continue growing at the rates they did in 2026, those technologies should counteract about 63 percent of the growth in emissions from 2025 to 2028 — or help avoid about 1.64 gigatons of added emissions.

The results indicate that the energy transition needs to accelerate if humankind is to realize consistently declining emissions, though EVs, solar and wind are already having a large impact. Without the offset in emissions provided by those technologies, global emissions would have risen by 1.9 percent each year on average from 2019 to 2025, the researchers note.

It’s very hard to say exactly how long it will take for humanity to reach peak emissions, Peters says. However, he notes, “the fact that we’re talking about this means that we’re close to that point.”
